newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END NARROWLY MIXED.
newsitem.headline: SINGAPORE GOVERNMENT SECURITIES END NARROWLY MIXED.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on Thursday on retail and interbank interest, dealers said.

"Government securities ended narrowly mixed today despite a small fall in the interbank rate. Treasury bill yields were slightly lower but bond prices were slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.20/2.15 percent compared with Wednesday's yield of 2.48/2.43 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.48/2.43 percent against 2.60/2.55 percent.
Among bonds, April 1999 ended at S$98.70/98.75 from Wednesday's close of S$98.65/98.70, May 2002 at S$99.70/99.75 versus S$99.63/99.68 and June 2003 at S$94.70/94.75 against S$94.65/94.70.
The overnight interbank offered rate fell to 1-1/2 1-3/8 percent from Wednesday's 2-1/8 2 percent.
